Density surfaces' slide-number: true echo: true lang: en --- ## {content-align="center" style="font-size: 150%;"}
**Spatial capture-recapture for
closed populations: Part II
Mapping density surfaces and activity centers**
::: {style='font-size: 60%;'} WILD(FISH) 8390
Inference for Models of Fish and Wildlife Population Dynamics
:::
# Overview {visibility="hidden"} ## Closed population model ::: {style='font-size: 50%;'} State model (a spatial point process model) $$ \lambda({\bf s}) = \exp(\beta_0 + \beta_1 w_1({\bf s}) + \beta_2 w_2({\bf s}) + \cdots) \\ \Lambda = \int_{\mathcal{S}} \lambda({\bf s}) \; \mathrm{d}{\bf s} \\ N \sim \mathrm{Pois}(\Lambda) \\ {\bf s}_i \propto \lambda({\bf s}) \;\; \mathrm{for}\; i=1,\dots,N $$ Observation model (supposing $N$ was known) $$ p_{ij} = g_0\exp(-\|{\bf s}_i - {\bf x}_j\|^2/(2\sigma^2)) \;\; \mathrm{for}\, j=1,\dots,J \\ y_{ijk} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_{ij}) $$ ::: ::: {style='font-size: 50%;'} $\lambda({\bf s})$ -- "Intensity function" describing expected density of individuals at location $\bf s$
$\Lambda$ -- Expected number of individuals in the spatial region $\mathcal{S}$
$N$ -- Realized number of individuals (ie, population size)
${\bf s}_i$ -- Location of the $i$th activity center
${\bf x}_j$ -- Location of trap $j$
$\|{\bf s}_i - {\bf x}_j\|$ -- Euclidean distance between ${\bf s}_i$ and ${\bf x}_j$
$g_0$ -- Capture probability when distance between activity centers and traps is 0
$\sigma$ -- Scale parameter of encounter function
$p_{ij}$ -- Capture probability
$y_{ijk}$ -- Spatial capture histories
::: ## Spatial point processes ::: {style='font-size: 90%;'}
The state model of SCR is a spatial (or spatio-temporal) point process.

::: {.fragment} There are many varieties of spatial point processes, including: - (In)homogeneous binomial point process - (In)homogeneous Poisson point process - Cox process - Gibbs process - Markov point process ::: ::: ## Spatial point processes ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} All share a few properties - The data are a collection of points called a "point pattern" - Points are in an area called the state-space ($\mathcal{S}$), or observation window, which is usually two dimensional - An intensity function, $\lambda({\bf s})$, describes spatial variation in the density of points - The area under this function is the expected number of points (a.k.a, $N$) in the region: $$ E(N) = \Lambda = \int_{\mathcal{S}} \lambda({\bf s}) \;\mathrm{d}{\bf s} $$ ::: ## Poisson point process ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} **Properties** - If density is constant throughout the state-space: $\lambda({\bf s}) = \lambda$, the process is said to be "homogeneous" - Otherwise, the process is "inhomogeneous" - The number of points in any region of the state-space is Poisson distributed - Points are independent of one another (no attraction or repulsion)
::: {.fragment}
An inhomogeneous point process allows for spatial variation in density, which can be modeled using [spatial covariates]{style="color: red;"}, such as raster layers.
::: ::: ## Density surfaces ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} We can use a fitted model to make maps of the following: 1. Expected density surface * This is an estimate of $\lambda({\bf s})$, the expected value of density at each location. * It's good for describing and predicting density at a different point in time. ::: {.fragment} 2. Realized density surface * Estimated number of activity centers per unit area [during the sampling period]{style="color: red;"}. ::: ::: {.fragment} 3. Activity center locations * The posterior distribution of each activity center. * This is not a home range map. ::: ::: # Simulation ## [Inhomogeneous Poisson point process]{style="font-size: 90%;"} ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} First, let's import a raster layer ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(raster) elevation <- raster("elevation.tif") delta <- res(elevation)[1] ## resolution plot(elevation, col=topo.colors(100), main="Elevation") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/ippp1-1.png){fig-align='center' width=45%} ::: ::: ::: ## [Inhomogeneous Poisson point process]{style="font-size: 90%;"} ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} Second, let's pick some coefficients and create a density surface ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} beta0 <- -15 beta1 <- 0.01 #0.005 lambda <- exp(beta0 + beta1*elevation) # Intensity function plot(lambda, col=terrain.colors(100), main="Density surface", zlim=c(0,0.18)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/ippp2-1.png){fig-align='center' width=45%} ::: ::: ::: ## [Inhomogeneous Poisson point process]{style="font-size: 90%;"} ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Third, simulate $N$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(538) ds <- 1 ## Pixel area is 1 ha lambda.values <- values(lambda) ## Convert raster to vector Lambda <- sum(lambda.values*ds) ## E(N) (N <- rpois(1, Lambda)) ## Realized N ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 98 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.fragment} Fourth, simulate ${\bf s}_1, \dots, {\bf s}_N$. To do this, we'll pick pixels proportional to density. Then we'll jitter each point inside its pixel. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} n.pixels <- length(lambda) jitter <- 0.005 ## Half width of pixel s.pixels <- sample(n.pixels, size=N, replace=TRUE, prob=lambda.values/Lambda) elevation.xyz <- as.data.frame(elevation, xy=TRUE) s <- elevation.xyz[s.pixels,c("x","y")] + cbind(runif(N, -jitter, jitter),runif(N, -jitter, jitter)) ``` ::: ::: ::: ## [Inhomogeneous Poisson point process]{style="font-size: 90%;"} ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(lambda, col=terrain.colors(100), main="Density surface with activity centers") points(s, pch=16, cex=1, col="blue") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/ippp5-1.png){fig-align='center' width=50%} ::: ::: ::: ## Traps ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- cbind(rep(seq(0.15, 0.85, by=0.1), each=8), rep(seq(0.15, 0.85, by=0.1), times=8)) ## Trap locations plot(lambda, col=terrain.colors(100), main="Density surface, activity centers and traps") points(s, pch=16, col="blue") ## Activity center locations points(x, pch=3) ## Trap locations ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/traps1-1.png){fig-align='center' width=45%} ::: ::: ::: ## [Distance b/w traps and activity centers]{style="font-size: 90%;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} J <- nrow(x) ## nTraps dist.sx <- matrix(NA, N, J) for(i in 1:N) { dist.sx[i,] <- sqrt((s[i,1]-x[,1])^2 + (s[i,2]-x[,2])^2) } ``` ::: ::: {.fragment} Look at distances between first 4 individuals and first 5 traps. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dist.sx[1:4,1:5] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [1,] 0.1218625 0.1175070 0.1810119 0.2678109 0.3614970 [2,] 0.9587743 0.8922040 0.8323508 0.7807610 0.7391668 [3,] 0.7162980 0.6912027 0.6800289 0.6834600 0.7012815 [4,] 0.6222620 0.5569781 0.5032288 0.4650310 0.4463949 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Capture probability ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Compute capture probability ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g0 <- 0.2 sigma <- 0.05 p <- g0*exp(-dist.sx^2/(2*sigma^2)) ``` ::: ::: {.fragment} Look at capture probs for first 4 individuals and first 5 traps. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} print(p[1:4,1:5], digits=3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [1,] 1.03e-02 1.26e-02 2.85e-04 1.18e-07 8.92e-13 [2,] 2.86e-81 1.44e-70 1.33e-61 2.25e-54 6.98e-49 [3,] 5.44e-46 6.36e-43 1.36e-41 5.34e-42 3.84e-44 [4,] 4.66e-35 2.27e-28 2.02e-23 3.29e-20 9.84e-19 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Capture histories ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Simulate capture histories for all $N$ individuals ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} K <- 5 # nOccasions y.all <- array(NA, c(N, J, K)) for(i in 1:N) { for(j in 1:J) { y.all[i,j,] <- rbinom(K, 1, prob=p[i,j]) } } ``` ::: ::: {.fragment} Discard individuals not captured ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} captured <- rowSums(y.all)>0 y <- y.all[captured,,] ``` ::: ::: ::: {.fragment} Capture histories for first 2 individuals and first 5 traps on first occasion. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} y[1:2,1:5,1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [1,] 0 0 0 0 0 [2,] 0 0 0 0 0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: # Likelihood ## R package 'secr' ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} Import data from two text files. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(secr) sch <- read.capthist(captfile="encounter_data_file.csv", trapfile="trap_data_file.csv", detector="proximity", fmt="trapID") ``` ::: ::: {.fragment} Create the "habitat mask", which defines the state-space and the spatial covariates. First, prepare the elevation covariate. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} elevation.xyz <- as.data.frame(elevation, xy=TRUE) elevation.xyz$y <- round(elevation.xyz$y, 3) ## Fix numerical fuzz elevation.xyz.m <- elevation.xyz elevation.xyz.m$x <- elevation.xyz$x*1000 ## Convert units to meters elevation.xyz.m$y <- elevation.xyz$y*1000 elevation.xyz.m$elevation <- scale(elevation.xyz$elevation) ## Standardize elevation.m <- rasterFromXYZ(elevation.xyz.m) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.fragment} Now create the mask. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(sp) elev.sp <- as(elevation.m, "SpatialGridDataFrame") trp <- traps(sch) mask <- make.mask(trp, buffer=150, spacing=10) mask <- addCovariates(mask, spatialdata=elev.sp) ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Habitat mask ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(mask, covariate="elevation") plot(trp, add=TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/plot-mask-1.png){fig-align='center' width=95%} ::: ::: ## R package 'secr' ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Model density as a function of elevation. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fm.elev <- secr.fit(sch, model=list(D=~elevation, g0=~1, sigma=~1), mask=mask, trace=FALSE) ## Don't use 'buffer' coef(fm.elev) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` beta SE.beta lcl ucl D -0.5600286 0.23323698 -1.0171647 -0.1028925 D.elevation 0.9419116 0.18885718 0.5717584 1.3120649 g0 -1.1779499 0.21368740 -1.5967695 -0.7591303 sigma 3.9089834 0.06556957 3.7804694 4.0374974 ``` ::: ::: Estimates on original scale (at average covariate values). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predict(fm.elev) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` link estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl D log 0.5712491 0.1350596 0.3616658 0.9022848 g0 logit 0.2354210 0.0384633 0.1684336 0.3188351 sigma log 49.8482523 3.2720450 43.8366152 56.6843093 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Estimated density surface ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} dsurf <- predictDsurface(fm.elev) dsurf.r <- raster(dsurf, covariate="D.0") pix.area <- (delta*1000)^2 plot(dsurf.r/pix.area, col=terrain.colors(100), zlim=c(0,0.18), main="Estimated density surface") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/secr-dsurf-1.png){fig-align='center' width=50%} ::: ::: ::: ## Estimated activity centers ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Contour map for the Empirical Bayes posterior distribution of the activity center for individual 1. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} fxiContour(fm.elev, i=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/fxi-1.png){fig-align='center' width=45%} ::: ::: ::: ## R package 'secr' We can still estimate $N$ as before. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} region.N(fm.elev) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl n E.N 87.3537 12.228402 66.48162 114.7786 59 R.N 87.3537 7.885437 75.60648 107.4108 59 ``` ::: ::: # Bayes ## SCR with data augmentation ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} Version 1: SCR model with inhomogeneous point process. $$ \lambda({\bf s}) = \exp(\beta_0 + \beta_1 \mathrm{ELEV}({\bf s})) \\ {\bf s}_i \propto \lambda({\bf s}) \\ \Lambda = E(N) = \int_{\mathcal{S}} \lambda({\bf s})\; \mathrm{d}{\bf s} \\ \psi = \Lambda/M \\ z_i \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\psi) \\ p_{ij} = g_0\exp(-\|{\bf s}_i-{\bf x}_j\|^2/(2\sigma^2)) \\ y_{ijk} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(z_i\times p_{ij}) \\ N=\sum_{i=1}^M z_i $$ This version is relatively slow and doesn't mix that well. ::: ## SCR with IPP -- version 1
[SCR-elev-v1.jag](SCR-elev-v1.jag)
::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` model { beta0 ~ dnorm(0, 0.1) beta1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.1) g0 ~ dunif(0, 1) sigma ~ dunif(0, 0.5) for(g in 1:G) { ## Loop over pixels lambda[g] <- exp(beta0 + beta1*elevation[g])*pixelArea pi[g] <- lambda[g]/Lambda } Lambda <- sum(lambda) EN <- sum(lambda) ## Expected value of N psi <- EN/M for(i in 1:M) { s[i,1] ~ dunif(xlim[1], xlim[2]) s[i,2] ~ dunif(ylim[1], ylim[2]) pixel[i] <- lookup[round((ylim[2]-s[i,2])/delta+0.5), ## row round((s[i,1]-xlim[1])/delta+0.5)] ## column logProb[i] <- log(pi[pixel[i]]) zeros[i] ~ dpois(-logProb[i]) ## zeros trick for IPP z[i] ~ dbern(psi) for(j in 1:J) { dist[i,j] <- sqrt((s[i,1]-x[j,1])^2 + (s[i,2]-x[j,2])^2) p[i,j] <- g0*exp(-dist[i,j]^2/(2*sigma^2)) } } for(i in 1:n) { ## Model for observed capture histories for(j in 1:J) { y.tilde[i,j] ~ dbinom(p[i,j], K) } } for(i in (n+1):M) { ## Model for augmented guys PrAtLeastOneCap[i] <- 1-prod(1-p[i,])^K zero.cap[i] ~ dbern(PrAtLeastOneCap[i]*z[i]) } N <- sum(z) } ``` ::: ::: ## SCR with data augmentation ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Version 2: SCR model with inhomogeneous point process $$ \tilde{\lambda}({\bf s}) = \exp(\beta_1 \mathrm{ELEV}({\bf s})) \\ {\bf s}_i \propto \tilde{\lambda}({\bf s}) \\ z_i \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\psi) \\ p_{ij} = g_0\exp(-\|{\bf s}_i-{\bf x}_j\|^2/(2\sigma^2)) \\ y_{ijk} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(z_i\times p_{ij}) \\ N=\sum_{i=1}^M z_i $$ This version is faster and mixes better. ::: ## SCR with IPP -- version 2 [SCR-elev-v2.jag](SCR-elev-v2.jag) ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` model { psi ~ dunif(0, 1) ## Can't put prior on psi *and* beta0 beta0 <- log(M*psi/Lambda) ## Algebra beta1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.1) g0 ~ dunif(0, 1) sigma ~ dunif(0, 0.5) for(g in 1:G) { ## Loop over pixels lambda[g] <- exp(beta1*elevation[g])*pixelArea pi[g] <- lambda[g]/Lambda } Lambda <- sum(lambda) EN <- M*psi for(i in 1:M) { s[i,1] ~ dunif(xlim[1], xlim[2]) s[i,2] ~ dunif(ylim[1], ylim[2]) pixel[i] <- lookup[round((ylim[2]-s[i,2])/delta+0.5), ## row round((s[i,1]-xlim[1])/delta+0.5)] ## column logProb[i] <- log(pi[pixel[i]]) zeros[i] ~ dpois(-logProb[i]) ## zeros trick for IPP z[i] ~ dbern(psi) for(j in 1:J) { dist[i,j] <- sqrt((s[i,1]-x[j,1])^2 + (s[i,2]-x[j,2])^2) p[i,j] <- g0*exp(-dist[i,j]^2/(2*sigma^2)) } } for(i in 1:n) { ## Model for observed capture histories for(j in 1:J) { y.tilde[i,j] ~ dbinom(p[i,j], K) } } for(i in (n+1):M) { ## Model for augmented guys PrAtLeastOneCap[i] <- 1-prod(1-p[i,])^K zero.cap[i] ~ dbern(PrAtLeastOneCap[i]*z[i]) } N <- sum(z) } ``` ::: ::: ## SCR with IPP -- version 3 ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} There's another version where we treat space as discrete, rather than continuous.
Under this formulation, activity centers are snapped to pixel centers, and a categorical prior is used instead of a continuous distribution.
This version is similar to what is used in likelihood-based methods.
It works fine, but it's slow in JAGS and it adds an extra level of approximation. ::: ## Inhomogeneous point process in JAGS ::: {style='font-size: 73%;'} We need to do the following to use version 2: - Provide the spatial covariate as a vector - Loop over all pixels to compute the *conditional*-on-$N$ density surface. - Retain the uniform prior on the activity centers, but add a second probability component to force them to be distributed according to the density surface. - This requires that we create a "lookup" table to map points in space to pixel IDs - Then we use the "zero's trick" to implement the non-standard probability distribution - Put a uniform prior on $\psi$.
::: {.fragment}
If we were using version 1, we would define $\psi=E(N)/M$ and we'd include $\beta_0$ in the intensity function.
::: ::: ## SCR with IPP ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} Create the lookup table ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} G <- nrow(elevation.xyz) ## nPixels lookup <- matrix(1:G, nrow=nrow(elevation), ncol=ncol(elevation), byrow=TRUE) ## To be consistent with raster package delta <- res(elevation)[1] ## resolution image(seq(delta/2, 1-delta/2, length=100), seq(delta/2, 1-delta/2, length=100), lookup, asp=1, xlab="x", ylab="y", frame=FALSE, col=0, main="Pixel ID") text(elevation.xyz$x[seq(5, G, by=10)], elevation.xyz$y[seq(5, G, by=10)], seq(5, G, by=10), cex=0.4) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/lookup-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: ## SCR with IPP ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} Data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} M <- 150 y.tilde <- apply(y, c(1,2), sum) n <- nrow(y) jags.data.SCR.elev <- list( y.tilde=y.tilde, n=n, M=M, J=J, G=G, delta=delta, lookup=lookup, pixelArea=delta^2*1e4, ## Convert to hectares elevation=elevation.xyz$elevation, z=c(rep(1, n), rep(NA, M-n)), zeros=rep(0, M), K=K, zero.cap=rep(0, M), x=x, xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1)) ``` ::: Inits and parameters ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} jp.SCR.elev <- c("beta0", "beta1", "g0", "sigma", "EN", "N") ji.SCR.elev <- function() { list(z=c(rep(NA, n), rep(0,M-n)),#psi=runif(1),beta0=runif(1,-20,-15), beta1=0.01, s=cbind(runif(M), runif(M)), g0=runif(1), sigma=runif(1, 0.05, 0.1)) } ``` ::: MCMC ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(jagsUI) jags.post.SCR.elev <- jags.basic( data=jags.data.SCR.elev, inits=ji.SCR.elev, parameters.to.save=jp.SCR.elev, model.file="SCR-elev-v2.jag", n.chains=3, n.adapt=100, n.iter=1000, parallel=TRUE) ``` ::: ::: ## Posterior summaries ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(jags.post.SCR.elev) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Iterations = 101:1100 Thinning interval = 1 Number of chains = 3 Sample size per chain = 1000 1. Empirical mean and standard deviation for each variable, plus standard error of the mean: Mean SD Naive SE Time-series SE EN 88.850648 10.474479 1.912e-01 0.5282427 N 88.959000 8.631733 1.576e-01 0.4805394 beta0 -14.443557 2.107711 3.848e-02 0.1669706 beta1 0.009138 0.001887 3.444e-05 0.0001482 g0 0.236503 0.039253 7.167e-04 0.0026025 sigma 0.050003 0.003434 6.270e-05 0.0002085 2. Quantiles for each variable: 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% EN 69.541232 81.586838 88.156952 95.47809 110.20447 N 74.975000 83.000000 88.000000 94.00000 109.00000 beta0 -18.451935 -15.929415 -14.411138 -12.97787 -10.27970 beta1 0.005432 0.007817 0.009106 0.01045 0.01273 g0 0.165442 0.209116 0.234794 0.26129 0.32409 sigma 0.043949 0.047650 0.049761 0.05217 0.05745 ``` ::: ::: ## Traceplots and density plots ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(jags.post.SCR.elev[,jp.SCR.elev[1:3]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/plot-mcmc-SCR-elev1-1.png){fig-align='center' width=70%} ::: ::: ## Traceplots and density plots ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(jags.post.SCR.elev[,jp.SCR.elev[4:6]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/plot-mcmc-SCR-elev2-1.png){fig-align='center' width=70%} ::: ::: ## Predicted density surface in JAGS ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Extract posterior samples of $\beta_0$ and $\beta_1$. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} beta.post <- as.matrix(jags.post.SCR.elev[,c("beta0","beta1")]) n.samples <- nrow(beta.post) ``` ::: Compute density surface for every MCMC sample ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lambda.post <- matrix(NA, n.pixels, n.samples) for(i in 1:n.samples) { lambda.post[,i] <- exp( beta.post[i,"beta0"] + beta.post[i,"beta1"]*elevation.xyz$elevation) } lambda.post.mean <- rowMeans(lambda.post) lambda.post.lower <- apply(lambda.post, 1, quantile, prob=0.025) lambda.post.upper <- apply(lambda.post, 1, quantile, prob=0.975) ``` ::: ::: ## Predicted density surface ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} Make multi-panel figure showing posterior mean density surface, along with 95% CI. ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} library(latticeExtra) trellis.par.set( regions=list( col=colorRampPalette(c("lightblue", "white", "orange", "firebrick"))(50))) ## Colors panel1 <- levelplot(lambda.post.lower ~ x+y, elevation.xyz, aspect="iso", at=seq(0,0.20,0.005), ## Resolution of color key colorkey=list(space="bottom"), xlab="", ylab="") panel2 <- levelplot(lambda.post.mean ~x+y, elevation.xyz, aspect="iso", at=seq(0,0.20,0.005)) panel3 <- levelplot(lambda.post.upper ~x+y, elevation.xyz, aspect="iso", at=seq(0,0.20,0.005)) panels <- c(panel1, panel2, panel3) panels <- update( panels, scales=list(draw=FALSE), layout=c(3,1), xlab="", ylab="", strip=strip.custom(bg=gray(0.8), factor.levels=c("Lower CI","Posterior mean","Upper CI"))) plot(panels) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/lambda-post-1.png){width=4000} ::: ::: ::: ## Realized density surface ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} We need to monitor $z$ and ${\bf s}_i$. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} jags.post.SCR.elev.sz <- jags.basic( data=jags.data.SCR.elev, inits=ji.SCR.elev, parameters.to.save=c(jp.SCR.elev,"s","z"), model.file="SCR-elev-v2.jag", n.chains=3, n.adapt=100, n.iter=2000, n.thin=2, parallel=TRUE) ``` ::: Extract posterior samples of $z$ and ${\bf s}_i$. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} s1.post <- as.matrix(jags.post.SCR.elev.sz[,paste0("s[", 1:M, ",1]")]) s2.post <- as.matrix(jags.post.SCR.elev.sz[,paste0("s[", 1:M, ",2]")]) z.post <- as.matrix(jags.post.SCR.elev.sz[,paste0("z[", 1:M, "]")]) ``` ::: Chop activity centers into discrete intervals, then tabulate. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lambda.r.post <- array(NA, c(sqrt(n.pixels), sqrt(n.pixels), n.samples)) for(i in 1:n.samples) { si1.post.d <- cut(s1.post[i,z.post[i,]==1], breaks=seq(0, 1, delta)) si2.post.d <- cut(s2.post[i,z.post[i,]==1], breaks=seq(0, 1, delta)) pixel.counts <- table(si2.post.d, si1.post.d) lambda.r.post[,,i] <- pixel.counts[sqrt(n.pixels):1,] } ``` ::: ::: ## Realized density surface ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} lambda.r.mean <- raster(apply(lambda.r.post, c(1,2), mean)) lambda.e.mean <- raster(matrix(lambda.post.mean, sqrt(n.pixels), byrow=TRUE)) lambda.re <- stack(lambda.r.mean, lambda.e.mean) names(lambda.re) <- c("Realized", "Expected") plot(lambda.re, zlim=c(0,0.18)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/lambda-r-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ## Posterior distribution of ***s***~*i*~ ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(x, asp=1, xlim=0:1, ylim=0:1, pch=3, axes=FALSE, ann=FALSE) points(s1.post[,1], s2.post[,1], pch=16, col=rgb(0,0,1,0.1)) contour(MASS::kde2d(s1.post[,1], s2.post[,1]), add=TRUE) points(x[y.tilde[1,]>0,,drop=FALSE], pch=3, col="red", lwd=2, cex=2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/si-post-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: ## Posterior distribution of ***s***~*i*~ ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/si-post-i-.gif){fig-align='center' width=50%} ::: ::: ::: ## Posterior distribution of _**s**~i~_ ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Posterior distribution of ${\bf s}_i$ for an indiviudal *not* captured. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} image(MASS::kde2d(s1.post[z.post[,150]==1,150], s2.post[z.post[,150]==1,150])) points(x, asp=1, pch=3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-cap-recap-spatial-II_files/figure-revealjs/si-post-y0-1.png){fig-align='center' width=45%} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ##points(s1.post[z.post[,150]==1,150], ## s2.post[z.post[,150]==1,150], pch=16, col=rgb(0,0,1,0.8)) ``` ::: ::: ## Summary ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Just as we can estimate both the realized and expected value of $N$, we can also estimate the realized and expected value of abundance (or density) at each location in the region of interest.
::: {.fragment} Sometimes, the region of interest will be different than $\cal S$, and we can easily obtain estimates of abundance in subsets of $\mathcal{S}$. :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
